Universidad César Vallejo|Universidad César Vallejo]] |league topscorer = [[Richard Estigarribia]] (23 goals) |biggest home win = [[Sport Huancayo]] 7-0 [[Club Coronel Bolognesi FC|Coronel Bolognesi]] |biggest away win = [[Club Sport Áncash|Sport Áncash]] 0-5 [[Sporting Cristal]] |highest scoring = [[Cienciano]] 5-5 [[Sporting Cristal]] |matches = 354 |total goals = 885 |prevseason = [[2008 Torneo Descentralizado|2008]] |nextseason = [[2010 Torneo Descentralizado|2010]] }} The '''2009 [[Torneo Descentralizado|Torneo Descentralizado de Fútbol Profesional]]''' (known as the '''Copa Cable Mágico''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 93rd season of [[Association football|Association]] Peruvian football. A total of 16 teams competed in the tournament. The season began on February 14 and concluded on December 13 with the victory of [[Universitario de Deportes]] over [[Alianza Lima]] in the second leg of the final Play-off, giving Universitario its twenty-fifth Peruvian title.{{cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=1148437.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091217091726/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=1148437.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 17, 2009 |title=World Leagues review |publisher=FIFA |access-date=April 26, 2010 |quote=It was also championship play-off day in Peru, where Universitario followed up their 1-0 defeat of old rivals Alianza Lima in the first leg with an identical result in the second. Veteran midfielder Nolberto Solano sparked jubilant scenes at the Estadio Monumental in Lima when he converted a penalty to end Universitario's nine-year title drought. }} ==Competitions modus== The season was divided into 3 stages. In the first stage the 16 teams played a round-robin home-and-away round for a total of 30 matches each. In the second stage the 16 teams were divided into 2 groups. The 8 teams that ranked an odd number played in the group Liguilla A and the 8 teams that ranked an even number played in Liguilla B. Each team carried on their records from the first stage. Each group played another round-robin home-and-away round for 14 matches played by each team. The teams ranked first in each group at the end of the 14 matches advanced to the third stage. The two teams with the worst fewest points at the end of the second stage were relegated. In the third stage the championship was contested in a two-legged Play-off. The Play-off finalists qualified for the [[Copa Libertadores]]. The remaining international competition berths were determined by the season aggregate table.{{cite web |url=http://www.adfp.org.pe/portal/archivos/bases/2009.pdf |title=Bases del Torneo Descentralizado 2009 |publisher=ADFP |pages=3–4 |language=es |format=PDF |access-date=June 6, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091122110242/http://www.adfp.org.pe/portal/archivos/bases/2009.pdf |archive-date=2009-11-22 |url-status=dead }} ==Changes from 2008== ===Structural changes=== *Two teams were added to the first division to make 16 teams in the first division from 14 in 2008. *The [[Apertura and Clausura]] tournament format was not used after the addition of the two teams to the first division. *Peru was given a third berth for the [[2010 Copa Sudamericana]]. *In the Play-off finals, goal difference was removed as a [[tiebreaker|tiebreaking]] criterion. A tie in points meant a third match at a neutral ground. ===Promotion and relegation=== [[Atlético Minero]] and [[Sport Boys]] finished the 2008 season in 13th and 14th place, respectively, in the aggregate table and thus were relegated to the [[Peruvian Segunda División|Segunda División]]. They were replaced by the champion and runner-up teams of the [[Segunda División Peruana 2008|2008 Segunda División]], [[Total Clean]] and [[Inti Gas Deportes|Inti Gas]] and champion and runner-up teams of the [[2008 Copa Perú]], [[Sport Huancayo]] and [[Colegio Nacional Iquitos|CNI]] ===Team changes=== {| class="wikitable" |- !
